prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Sentinel Vale: EO mission (land/coastal/cryosphere). External: spacecraft, launch segment, user processing environments, conjunction data source, users. Security: least privilege, strong auth, segmentation, audit. Mission Control Center (Bluebell): real-time authority, pass supervision, anomaly response, contact schedule, routing policy; gets command prep package from MPS, sends constraints to MPS; declares continuity modes (objective, duration, exit criteria); must show continuous console coverage and complete handover logs. Uplink needs MCC + Spacecraft Operations Team (SOT) concurrence. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey): rejects commands unapproved, unprovenanced, expired, out-of-window, or lacking authorization state, validation result, operator acknowledgment; accepts Star Tracker Mask File only if integrity, config ID, approval match baseline. Cybersecurity Desk: exceptions, daily privileged-access review, public interface changes; validates alert routing and incident coordination in final exercise. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral): ephemerides/events to MCC, MPS, PPF; mask file; orbit quality state to archive; shows orbit/screening/conjunction within planning cycle. Flight Dynamics Team: screening, maneuver recommendation to SOT, Ephemeris Delta Note (MPS applies in schedule validation); rehearses missed tracking/late orbit update. Orbit Determination Engine: Doppler Residual Report, Laser Retroreflector Window (to MPS). Mission Planning System (Cedar): authoritative timeline; suspends auto publication on anomaly. Network Control System (Lantern): routing, Security Exception Ticket; records rehearsals (maintenance, station loss, degraded routing, restoration). Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse): Primary/Backup Processing Clusters; quarantine unproven lineage; product package, quality metadata, checksums to archive; sustained generation without unapproved manual action. Backup takeover after custody, baseline, authorization verified; Backup uses Storage Watermark Snapshot to confirm capacity before standby. Ground Network Manager: cross-site failover; antenna baseline needs current maintenance clearances for North/South S-Band, Kiruna/Svalbard X-Band Antennas. Telemetry Ingest Service: Pass Replay Packet to SOT. SOT: day-in-the-life rehearsal. Payload Calibration Team: reprocessing requests; traceable quality criteria. Product Quality Service: quality flags, Product Hold List (USP blocks release until cleared). Long Term Archive (Granite): custody reference; catalogue to User Services Portal; Storage Watermark Snapshot; reconciles delayed ingest; preserves baseline, retrieval

Document units:
S244: Operational key performance indicators include contact success rate, telemetry completeness, command validation timeliness, product latency, product quality disposition time, archive availability, help desk responsiveness, and unresolved anomaly age.
S245: Each key performance indicator has an assigned data source, sampling interval, review owner, threshold, and corrective action trigger so that routine reporting does not depend on informal judgment.
S246: The primary monthly service review compares actual performance against the accepted baseline and records trend explanations for any measure that moves outside the watch band.
S247: The Primary Processing Cluster and Backup Processing Cluster are baselined with approved software versions, processing configurations, capacity reservations, monitoring checks, and rollback instructions before handover.
S248: Configuration baselines for ground software, operational procedures, interface control data, account roles, and monitoring rules are frozen at readiness review entry and changed only through approved change control.
S249: Handover to routine mission service is authorized when acceptance evidence is complete, rehearsals meet their objectives, open risks are acknowledged by accountable owners, and support teams confirm on-call coverage.
S250: After handover, the first operational reporting cycle is treated as a stabilization period in which deviations are reviewed daily and permanent process changes are deferred until sufficient evidence is available.
